lines: Ever noticed the tiny ridges on the edge of some coins?
They're called reeding. And they once stopped a crime wave.
Smooth. Shiny. What could go wrong?
Back then, coins were made of real silver. So people shaved tiny slivers off the edges.
Collect enough shavings, melt them down... free silver!
And the clipped coin? Still spent at full value.
Soon, so many coins were clipped that nobody trusted money anymore.
It got so bad, clipping coins was high treason. You could be executed for it.
The fix? Ridges on the edge. Shave one, and everybody can see it.
And in [1696|sixteen ninety-six], the man hunting counterfeiters for the Royal Mint? Isaac Newton. Yes, the gravity guy.
Today, coins are mostly cheap metal. But the ridges stayed... and now they help blind people tell coins apart by touch.
So... what should I delete next?
